hook: There’s a note sewn into the wedding dress.
excerpt: She eased the lining back from the seam allowance.

excerpt.text: There was something underneath it that shouldn’t have been there.

excerpt: The strip came away in her fingers, a little stiff, about the length of her hand.
She unfolded it under the lamp.

excerpt.text: Pencil. Gone soft and grey with time, in a hand that pressed hard and leaned forward, the downstrokes almost through the cloth.
If you’re wearing this, he’s done it again.

excerpt: She read it twice. Then a third time, more slowly, as if the words might rearrange themselves into something to do with hooks and eyes.

excerpt.text: It wasn’t written to her. It was written to whoever was wearing the dress, and in nine days that would be a woman who had stood on that box an hour ago and called it a costume.

caption:
There’s a note sewn into the wedding dress.

For twenty-two years, Nell has altered other people’s dresses in her Bath workroom and never asked why. Then she opens a seam on the Lyall family’s gown, nine days before the wedding.

Under the Lining is out now in Kindle and paperback. Link in bio. 🧵
